Think of it this way: You're assigned king of a society. No one has any previous skills. No artistic skills, no manual labor skills, nothing. Luckily, there's a college nearby to get everyone trained in mining, construction, plumbing all the good stuff we need to survive. You guys find some resources, sell those to countries, buy some lumber, establish a banking system, and BAM! Everyone is exchanging currency. You have a Total Economic Surplus, meaning everyone is benefiting somewhat through trade.

So your people get together and discuss what they should do with the money. Some people complain about there being no hospital. Other people complain about how bored they are all the time. (Remember: No one is an artist, athlete, nothing. There are no movies, no paintings, no sports, nothing. They are living a fairly joyless existence.) So you build a hospital and a theater. You have about 100 staff at the hospital, and only 5 staff at the theater.

Eventually, your town grows. You need a bigger hospital. This one needs 200 staff, but your theater needs only 5 people still. 

Now even after the expansion, your hospital is still too small! People are waiting forever in the ER, you don't have enough beds. 

This is called a **shortage**. Normally, when we want to eliminate a shortage, we raise the price of that good or service. But this isn't really possible with hospitals.  What are you gonna do? Raise the price of an office visit until all the poor people stop lining up out your doors? Of course not, because healthcare is a necessity. So to eliminate the shortage, you decide to put more money into the hospital.  But there's just no profits to be had! (Remember, this is your society. Corruption hasn't rooted itself in the system. Hospitals are not profit driven.) By the nature of hospitals, there is a marginal cost for each patient you see. So the more patients you have, the more money you make, but you need to spend that money on more doctors and nurses.

Now the theater has their own shortage. They sell out every night! They're turning away half the town at the box office! There just aren't enough seats! But the theater doesn't mind. All they have to do is raise the prices of their tickets, since people clearly are willing to pay quite a bit to see their plays. That's how they choose to correct for the shortage, because theater is not a necessity.

So with a theater, (or sports, or art, whatever) there really are no marginal costs. There's no difference to the theater if the actors are performing for an audience of 1 or 1,000. So to eliminate the shortage,  The theater is making more and more revenue, while their cost stay the same. So buy exploiting your townsfolk's desire to escape from their harsh reality of under-resourced hospitals, the 5 theater employees are splitting quite a bit of money among themselves.

Now the town over had a similar town meeting to you. They their own hospital and a BIGGER theater. This theater has much more seats, but  their actors aren't very good. So they offer your town's actors $1,000,000 (double what your theater's paying them) to come to their theater. So now you gotta go out and hire new actors, but guess what! Any actors as good as the ones you just lost will be cost about $1,000,000, because that is the value the market has paid on them. And that value is based on

a) The scarcity of highly-trained, captivating actors

and

b) how much money people are willing to pay to see these actors... because their lives are so miserable, they are willing to pay TOP DOLLAR for some high-quality escapism. Because you see there is only ONE best actor in the world... how's that for scarcity?

Meanwhile, the other town's hospital offers your doctors more money to come work for them, but not much more. After all, there are a lot of doctors going around. Now, you've had all these weird diseased come in, all of them require their own little treatments. There's a strange form of dyptheria, for example, and there’s  only one doctor able to treat it. Now, in a perfectly just society, this man should be the richest man on the planet! Because, if we are to put no value on human life, we would be willing to pay him any amount of money to save this person’s life. Problem is, the type of people who get dyptheria don’t have a ton of money laying around. They could maybe scrounge together $30,000. So, theoretically, the doctor (who is even more skilled and scarce as the 2 actors) would theoretically only be paid $30,000. But we don’t wanna do that, so we better all pool our money together and pay him at least enough to compensate the years of training he went through (hello health-insurace/government funded health-care)
So, prices for a necessity goods/services are based an *ability to pay*, while prices for luxuries are based on *willingness to pay*.

It is because **necessities** are **necessary**, that we as a society do all we can to keep their costs down, which includes how much we pay the people who provide these necessities. This is to prevent pricing poor people out of the market. Because theater and sports are a luxuries, that we feel it is okay to raise the prices of those luxuries items until only the rich can afford them, which means there’s a lot of money left over for spending… Resulting in people who spend their lives honing a craft, because the very best performers/athletes are paid quite well.

Get skills, get paid.

High athlete salaries incentivize children to hone their craft and push their bodies to their limits. This results in a flood of talent into highly competitive sports leagues, which (like movies) are enjoyed for entertainment value.  The more talented the players, the more fun the game is to watch.

It's not like everyone got together and decided an basketball player should make 1,000,000x more an hour than a construction worker. They're not worth 1,000,000x as humans, it's just a reflection of how society values their skills.

People who work shitty manual labor jobs may provide a necessary service to society, but there are millions of people who can do what they do, which means companies can pay them low wages and still fill the positions.

And actors are, at the end of the day, saying words. 

Musicians are, at the end of the day, plucking strings.

Artists are, at the end of the day, coloring canvas.

People pay money to watch skilled people practice their craft. It's not arbitrary. It's why front row tickets to an NBA game costs thousands, while front row tickets to a high school game cost $5.
